# Plan: Build and evaluate the triage agent with the SPE loop

## Core point

The spec says "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." That spec cannot be measured yet. Step 1 turns it into numbers. Step 2 freezes my predictions before anything runs. The evals then test those predictions. I will make one local commit after each step. I will not push.

I am reading SPE as Spec, Predict, Evaluate. This plan is the first Predict. Please correct me if your loop defines the letters differently.

## Questions I need answered before step 3

1. **Ticket source.** Where do the tickets come from? Examples are Jira, a help desk, or email. I will only read from that system. I will not change it.
2. **Labeled examples.** Do you have tickets that a person has already triaged? Real labels are the strongest test. If I write the tickets and the labels myself, the agent is graded against my own guesses. That is circular. I would use synthetic tickets only as a smoke test.
3. **What "triage" outputs.** I propose three fields: category, priority, and route (team or queue). Please give the allowed values for each.
4. **What "cheaply" means.** I need a budget per ticket. A dollar ceiling or a token ceiling both work.
5. **Models.** Which models may the agent use? A cheaper model may meet the budget. I will only test the models you name.
6. **Language.** I will match the repo's main language. I will confirm it before I write code.

## Spec (proposed numbers for you to accept or change)

| Criterion | Proposed bar | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|
| Category correct | 90% or higher | Exact match against the human label |
| Priority correct | 80% or higher | Exact match |
| Severe miss | 0 cases | The agent rates a top-priority ticket two or more levels low |
| Route correct | 90% or higher | Exact match |
| Cost | At or under your budget per ticket | Tokens logged per call, converted to dollars from the current pricing page at run time |
| Stability | The same answer in at least 2 of 3 runs | Each case runs 3 times |

## Prediction 1 (frozen in step 2, before any run)

All numbers below are estimates. The evals exist to prove them wrong.

- A v0 agent with one prompt and the label list will score 80% to 90% on category.
- Priority will be the weakest field. It will score 65% to 80%. Most misses will fall between adjacent levels.
- Severe misses will be rare but not zero in v0.
- The agent will put too many tickets in "other" or "general" when that bucket exists.
- Tickets that raise two issues at once will cause most of the category misses.
- Cost will be driven by input length. Long email threads will cost the most. Trimming quoted replies will cut cost more than any prompt change.
- A cheaper model will lose more points on priority than on category.

**Falsifiers.** Any of these results means my model of the problem is wrong:
- v0 category accuracy below 70%.
- Priority scoring higher than category.
- Cost driven mainly by output tokens.

## Folder layout

```
spe/
  triage/
    spec.md            the measurable spec
    predictions.md     dated predictions, never edited after a run
    log.md             one entry per loop: prediction, result, gap, next change
    evals/
      cases.jsonl      ticket text plus the expected labels
      holdout.jsonl    cases the agent is never tuned on
      grade            deterministic grader script
    agent/
      prompt.md        the system prompt
      triage           the agent entry point
    runs/
      <date>-v0/       raw outputs, scores, token counts
```

## Steps

Each step ends with one local commit. Commit messages describe the change only.

| Step | Work | Commit message |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Create the `spe/triage/` skeleton above with empty files | `chore(spe): scaffold triage SPE folder` |
| 1 | Write `spec.md` with the numbers you approve | `docs(spe): define measurable triage spec` |
| 2 | Write `predictions.md` with Prediction 1 and its falsifiers | `docs(spe): record prediction 1` |
| 3 | Build the eval set. Split it into a tuning set and a holdout set. Target is at least 100 cases if real data exists. | `test(spe): add triage eval cases` |
| 4 | Write the grader. It does exact match and confusion matrices, logs tokens, and does no LLM judging. | `test(spe): add deterministic triage grader` |
| 5 | Build the v0 agent. It is one prompt with structured output and no tools. | `feat(spe): add triage agent v0` |
| 6 | Run the eval workflow on v0 (see below) | `test(spe): record v0 eval run` |
| 7 | Compare the results to Prediction 1 in `log.md`. Write Prediction 2 for one change. | `docs(spe): log v0 results and prediction 2` |
| 8+ | Repeat steps 5 to 7. Each loop makes exactly one change. | `feat(spe): triage agent vN <change>` |

## The eval workflow (runs after you approve)

1. It loads the tuning set and the agent version under test.
2. It runs each case 3 times in parallel batches.
3. It saves the raw output, input tokens, output tokens, and latency per call.
4. The grader scores each field against the label.
5. The grader builds a confusion matrix for category, priority, and route.
6. The grader lists every severe miss by ticket ID.
7. It converts tokens to cost with the current pricing for each model.
8. It writes a pass or fail line for each spec criterion.
9. It runs the holdout set only when the tuning set passes. A holdout failure means the agent was overfit.

## Stop rules

- **Done.** All spec criteria pass on the holdout set.
- **Stop and ask.** Three loops in a row fail to improve the weakest criterion.
- **Stop and ask.** Correct and cheap conflict, and no tested model meets both bars. You decide the trade.

## Limits I will keep

- I will make local commits only. I will not push, open a PR, or merge.
- The ticket system stays read-only.
- Commits carry no Claude attribution.
- Ticket text that contains customer data stays out of commits until you confirm it may be stored in this repo.
- I will not edit `predictions.md` after a run. Wrong predictions stay on the record.

## Unverified in this plan

- I have not looked at the repo. The folder layout and language are assumptions.
- All accuracy figures are estimates. I have not run anything.
- I will check cost figures against current pricing at run time. I have not looked them up yet.
critiques: The Spec table turns "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" into criteria with numeric bars. Examples are "Category correct 90% or higher" and "Severe miss 0 cases". Each row has a "How it is measured" column that names the test, such as exact match against the human label or tokens logged per call.

Prediction 1 is a bulleted list, not a table. Only v0 category and priority get number ranges. The cheaper-model configuration is described as "will lose more points on priority". Severe misses are "rare but not zero", and cost has no number. These are adjectives, not numbers.
The predicted ranges, such as "80% to 90% on category" and "65% to 80%" on priority, have no stated reason. No bullet explains why that number was chosen.
Step 2 writes and commits predictions.md before the eval run in step 6. The plan never saves a copy of itself to a file or commits one.
The eval workflow loads cases, runs them, grades them, and gates the holdout on the tuning set passing. It has no grader selftest and no small dry run before the full run.

The grader produces exact-match scores, confusion matrices, a severe-miss list, and token counts. Several predictions have no named check. Examples are "Tickets that raise two issues at once will cause most of the category misses" and the claim that trimming quoted replies cuts cost. No case tagging or ablation measures these.
Step 7 says "Compare the results to Prediction 1 in log.md. Write Prediction 2 for one change." Step 8+ then repeats the loop. This is a close-out that seeds the next round.
